channels.name: Direct operations
lines: Our people run the floor on our phones: anchors, supervisors, and a Portfolio Manager.
Everything below is done by us.

channels.name: Delivery partner
channels.who: The partner, to our standards, on our phones
lines: The partner hires and runs their own team on our phones. We take the final hours from them.
They sign the standard agreement and follow every step below. Nobody skips one.

steps.title: Find the site
steps.done: A meeting is booked with someone who can say yes.
lines: We keep a list of the kinds of places we want to film in, ranked by the task types we need more of, with the upload path in mind.
We reach out through people we know and by walking in.
Anyone who brings a site that signs gets a 10% referral reward. Portfolio Managers source for their own books and earn the same.

steps.title: Close the deal
steps.who: Mano handles the paperwork, and Moharam handles the operational details.
steps.done: The agreement is signed, access is confirmed, and the payment terms are with Mano.
lines: We meet the owner, walk the floor, and agree what we film and what we pay.
We sign the participation agreement and agree on signage and consent.
We set access hours, who may enter, and the site's safety rules.

steps.title: Visit the filming location
steps.who: Mazen, Moharam, and the site's Portfolio Manager
steps.done: A site plan: zones, power, storage, upload path, shift pattern.
lines: We walk the whole site: where we record, where we never record, where the power is, where the gear lives.
We confirm how footage gets out: the site's own fiber, or a runner to one of our hubs.
We agree the safety rules and the protective gear for that floor.

steps.title: Central planning
steps.done: A dispatch schedule: which phones leave inventory on which day, and which site they go to.
lines: Central planning reads the dashboard: how many floors are active, when each project ends, when phones and people come free, and how many workers are free.
From that it writes the dispatch schedule. For example: take 40 phones from inventory on day X and deploy them to the site on day Y.
It sends the order to procurement: these phones, these caps, and everything else the site needs.

steps.title: Provide and hand out the gear
steps.done: The Portfolio Manager has every phone, cap, and mount on the schedule.
lines: Mazen gets the order from central planning and provides the phones, the caps, the mounts, the chargers, and the spares.
He hands the gear to the site's Portfolio Manager on the day the schedule says.
The Portfolio Manager then screens every worker before anyone puts on a phone.

steps.title: Screen every worker
steps.done: Every wearer has papers on file and one account in their own name.
lines: The site suggests the person. The Portfolio Manager approves them.
A copy of their ID, a signed consent form, and the fraud briefing signed off.
One account per person, in their own name. Never shared, never reused.

steps.title: Day 0
steps.done: Pilot footage checked, and Moharam certifies the launch.
lines: Set up the charging stations and the device room.
Label every phone and mount. Test the network from the floor.
Show every wearer the angle, the 30-minute cycle, and that hat off means tap stop first.
Run pilot recordings and check them for angle and lighting before the first real hour.

steps.title: Film
steps.who: The Portfolio Manager and the anchors
steps.done: Hours land on target with clean footage, every day.
lines: Wearers rotate so nobody sits on one task all week.
30-minute cycles, restarted on time.
Charging, custody, clock-in and clock-out, every day.
No phone sleeps holding more than a day of footage.

steps.title: Check in on the site
steps.done: The site has been seen today, at a time nobody expected.
lines: The Portfolio Manager drops in unannounced, at a different time each day.
First week after launch: two or three visits a day. Second week: one or two a day. After that: at least once a day.
On each visit they check the camera angles, the 30-minute cycle, charging, custody, and how the wearers are doing.

steps.title: Upload
steps.who: The runner, sent by the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: Every phone has uploaded at a hub before the next shift starts.
lines: Most sites will not have fiber. So every night the phones go to an upload hub and upload over fiber there.
There is one central hub downtown and two satellite hubs, one in Sheikh Zayed and one in the Fifth Settlement. A site uses whichever is closest.
The runner takes the phones in several runs, never all of them in one vehicle, and brings them back before the shift.
This is the current plan. It may still change.

steps.title: Review every video
steps.who: Youssef Medhat's team, with the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: Flags fall week over week, and the client has no surprises.
lines: Our own team watches every video before the client sees it: keep, flag, or delete.
A flag goes to the Portfolio Manager the same day and to the worker within 24 hours, with the fix.
Three flags pulls the worker. Two strikes pauses the device until they are retrained.
Review corrects filming, every day.

steps.title: Report the number
steps.who: Portfolio Managers to Mano, then the executive sync
steps.done: The number is on the dashboard before the executive sync.
lines: Every Portfolio Manager sends the wrap report: hours, active phones, hardware, problems, fixes.
Mano consolidates it into one company number every evening.
Adham, Moharam, and Mano review every site against quota, move phones and people where the hours are, and clear the day's escalations.

steps.title: Month-end audit
steps.done: Flagged footage deleted, the clean total agreed.
lines: The audit passes run before anything is invoiced.
Flagged footage is deleted and never invoiced.

steps.title: Get paid on accepted hours, net of fraud flags
steps.done: Everyone in the chain is paid on the same number.
lines: The client pays for the hours it accepts, and flagged hours come off first.
Sites, workers, staff, and partners are paid the same way, on the same number.

questions.q: Will the owner run the floor with their own people, on our phones?
Do we have a Portfolio Manager and anchors in that city?
Does the site have fiber, or a hub within reach?
Can a partner staff it and deliver hours to our standards?

outcomes.name: Direct operations
outcomes.text: Adham closes. Mazen runs Day 0 with the Portfolio Manager. Moharam certifies the launch.

outcomes.name: Delivery partner
outcomes.text: Adham signs the standard agreement. Phones leave enrolled. Central planning sets the phones. Moharam certifies the site and runs the relationship day to day.

outcomes.name: Not yet
outcomes.text: On the target list with Mano. Source a hub or a partner first, then ask again.
